tags.name: wire
tags.description: Wire.js reactive element. Renders from signals/expressions. Content attributes `for` and `to` are mutually exclusive.

attributes.name: to
attributes.description: Directly render a value as the element's HTML. Takes a signal (`@name`) or expression (`{{ expr }}`). Cannot be used if the element has HTML content; mutually exclusive with `for`.

attributes.name: with
attributes.description: Re-render the element's HTML template whenever this signal (`@name`) changes. Signal only.

attributes.name: for
attributes.description: Render the element's HTML template once per item of a list. Takes a signal (`@name`) or expression (`{{ expr }}`) yielding an array. Mutually exclusive with `to`.

attributes.name: each
attributes.description: Name of the variable that holds the current item inside a `for` template. Literal only; requires `for`.

attributes.name: if
attributes.description: Only render when truthy. Takes a signal (`@name`) or expression (`{{ expr }}`). Reference a signal (e.g. with `with`) so it re-evaluates.

attributes.name: style
attributes.description: Inline style applied to the element. Literal only.

tags.name: component
tags.description: Wire.js component. Without `instance` it defines a template (declared args via `arg:name`); with `instance` it renders that template.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Component name. Required. Used to register a template, or to select which template an instance renders.

attributes.name: instance
attributes.description: Marks this element as an instance of the named component instead of a template definition. Flag attribute.

attributes.name: arg:
attributes.description: Component argument, written `arg:<name>`. On a template definition it is a bare flag declaring an argument (e.g. `arg:title`); on an instance it takes a literal, signal (`@name`) or expression (`{{ expr }}`) value. Use `{{name}}` inside the template to read it.

attributes.name: style
attributes.description: Inline style applied to the element. Literal only.
